text: dsh-fnos-control 是面向 fnOS 上 DSH Web 的网页插件，会在 DSH 侧栏加入服务控制面板。面板可查看服务进程、端口及网关状态，刷新当前页面，或请求重启 DSH Web；重启后会等待服务恢复并自动刷新。fnOS 环境下通过应用网关控制接口工作，独立运行时使用辅助进程重启。适合在飞牛 NAS 上管理 DSH 网页服务；无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-fnos-control adds a service panel to the DSH web sidebar for fnOS. It shows DSH Web and gateway status, reloads the page, or requests a service restart and reloads after recovery. On fnOS it uses the app gateway; standalone mode uses a helper process. No API key is required.
想从 DSH 网页里直接重启飞牛 NAS 上托管的 DSH Web 服务。
有没有办法在侧栏查看服务状态并快速刷新当前 DSH 页面？
I want to restart my fnOS-managed DSH web service from its control panel and have the page reload when it comes back.
dsh-fnos-control 的功能「网页服务状态」：侧栏中的服务控制面板读取 DSH Web 的进程、端口和网关状态，并定期刷新状态信息。打开面板后会立即读取，每 15 秒更新一次。
dsh-fnos-control 的功能「重启与恢复」：用户在面板二次确认后请求重启 DSH Web；fnOS 下交由网关控制，独立运行时使用辅助进程。面板轮询服务恢复状态，恢复后自动刷新页面。

dsh-fnos-control README · dsh-fnos-control：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin for **fnOS (飞牛 OS)**. It adds one sidebar entry — **Service Control** — with a single panel offering the two operations the fnOS application already ships, without the keyboard shortcut hunt:

dsh-fnos-control README · dsh-fnos-control：| Action | What it really does |
|---|---|
| **Reload page** | `location.reload()` — the same thing as the app's `F5` / `Ctrl+R`. The process is untouched. |
| **Restart DSH Web** | Asks the fnOS gateway to stop and start the supervised `dsh web` child process, then waits for recovery and reloads the page. |
dsh-fnos-control README · Live site：The project page is published at **https://dsh.likkas.cn/**.

dsh-fnos-control README · Why this plugin exists：The fnOS application (`fn-deepseek-harness`) runs `dsh web` as a child of its gateway (`gateway-proxy.mjs`). The gateway already publishes a control API on its unix socket:

```
GET  /app/fn-deepseek-harness/__fnos-gateway/control/web/status
POST /app/fn-deepseek-harness/__fnos-gateway/control/web/restart
```

dsh-fnos-control README · Why this plugin exists：`restart` stops the child, starts it again with the original arguments, waits for the port to pass its health check, then refreshes `app.pid` and the launch token. That is the correct supervisor to ask — restarting "yourself" from inside a supervised process loses the supervisor's handshake. This plugin wraps that path in a UI, and keeps a standalone detached-helper fallback for hosts with no fnOS gateway (for example a plain `dsh web` started by hand).

dsh-fnos-control README · Direct download：A built tarball is attached to [release v0.1.0](https://github.com/QICci/dsh-fnos-control/releases/tag/v0.1.0);
the project site (`site/index.html`) exposes it behind a slide-to-download control so a stray click never
starts a transfer. The published file is `dsh-fnos-control-0.1.0.tgz`
(SHA-256 `ebd31664752bba3139e12c02e5d31283ac7ce3d31cae87b71912958f20d7fb2a`).
Verify a download with `node package/scripts/smoke.mjs` before installing.

dsh-fnos-control README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` (verified on `0.2.1-rc.3`)
- Node.js `>= 20`
- fnOS application `fn-deepseek-harness` for the gateway restart path. Without it the panel still renders and the helper fallback is used.

dsh-fnos-control README · From this directory (development / local checkout)：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-fnos-control
```

Then make sure the bundle is applied — adding it through the plugin manager does this automatically:

```bash

dsh-fnos-control README · From a tarball：```bash
tar -xzf dsh-fnos-control-0.1.0.tar.gz
dsh plugin --profile web add ./package
```

dsh-fnos-control README · Listing it in the profile：`dsh plugin add` appends the bundle name to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json`. If you install by hand, add `dsh-fnos-control` there yourself:

```json
{ "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["...", "dsh-fnos-control"] } } }
```

Do **not** also insert the same row into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: one row, one mount, otherwise boot fails with a duplicate loader entry id.

dsh-fnos-control README · What it adds：**Sidebar entry** — `sidebar.panellist` id `fnos-control`, order `60`, label from the plugin's locale (`服务控制` / `Service Control`).

**Main panel** — `main` slot keyed `fnos-control`, so the sidebar button opens it.

**Host routes** (both require the `x-dsh-control: 1` header and answer loopback peers only):

dsh-fnos-control README · What it adds：| Route | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/dsh-fnos-control/api/status` | `GET` | Serving PID, port, origin, argv, gateway socket reachability and state, PID recorded by the gateway, detected supervisor. |
| `/dsh-fnos-control/api/restart` | `POST` | Schedules the restart: gateway path when the fnOS socket exists, detached-helper path otherwise. Refuses under systemd and under a debugger. |

dsh-fnos-control README · Safety model：- Restart is a two-step click (confirm within 5 seconds).
- The restart route accepts `POST` only, loopback only, with the package's own header — a cross-site form or image cannot send it.
- The Host half never restarts when it detects a systemd unit (the detached helper would die with the cgroup) and reports why instead.
- The page polls for recovery: gateway mode reads `/__fnos-gateway/control/web/status` until `running`; direct mode probes the page URL. Timeout is 90 seconds, after which the panel tells you to reload manually.
- Nothing is written to disk by the plugin itself.

dsh-fnos-control README · Verification：```bash
node --check index.js && node --check client.js
curl -s -H 'x-dsh-control: 1' http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-fnos-control/api/status
```

The status route answering with your PID and the gateway state means the Host half is mounted. The sidebar entry appears after the page loads the plugin's client bundle.
